cases.name: choose-role-decision-for-judgment
cases.trap: Use an expensive runtime case or require tool calls when the contract is only the role's decision.
cases.prompt: Reviewer has a contract change: when supplied implementation evidence directly violates an accepted behavioral requirement, Reviewer must return a failing review rather than approve it or invent new product meaning. We want a focused behavioral regression test. The tool sequence is not part of the contract. Design the case and choose the execution mode.
expectations: Chooses role-decision because the load-bearing evidence is Reviewer's judgment and next production decision, not a real tool sequence.

Builds a realistic supplied requirement plus contradictory implementation/evidence scenario and names the plausible trap, such as approving despite the contradiction or inventing replacement product meaning.
Grades the decision/outcome rather than exact verdict prose or magic phrases.
Does not require runtime tool/action assertions in role-decision mode.
Keeps the production requirement/authority contract outside the eval and treats the case only as verification.
Notes that separate runtime coverage would be needed if the claim later expands to actual assessment tool use or workflow-state mutation.
negative_expectations: Must not choose runtime solely because it seems more realistic when no runtime behavior is part of the claim.
Must not require Reviewer to call tools that the selected mode deliberately denies.

cases.name: choose-runtime-for-recovery-execution
cases.trap: Accept a model statement that recovery happened without proving the required production actions against workflow state.
cases.prompt: A past recovery bug looked fine in chat: General said it had continued an exhausted Worker budget and resumed the task, but no Worker was actually dispatched or attached. The production contract requires recovery to continue the budget, inspect state, grant dispatch, dispatch Worker, and attach it to the existing workflow. Design the regression eval.
expectations: Chooses runtime because the regression is about actual Loom/OpenCode actions and workflow state, not merely a stated decision.
Uses disposable seeded workflow state that represents the exhausted-but-unfinished condition instead of asking the model to imagine it.
Requires observed actions for budget continuation, state inspection, dispatch grant, Worker dispatch, and attachment bound to the intended existing workflow.
Rejects replacement work, stopping after budget mutation, or prose that merely claims recovery succeeded.
Keeps the expensive runtime case focused and opt-in when appropriate rather than turning unrelated cheap cases into runtime tests.
Treats provider or harness failure as non-evidence rather than a semantic FAIL.
negative_expectations: Must not use role-decision or final output text as sufficient proof that Worker was actually dispatched and attached.
Must not seed the desired recovery result itself; setup may create the precondition but production tools must perform recovery.
